LESSON: FOLDING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.2: Folding
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Folding, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: How does folding influence our day-to- day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm on the meaning of folding and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views. Those with postural difficulties could require appropriate positioning,

2. Discuss types of folds resulting from tectonic forces and make presentations in class,

3. use print or digital resources to research on the resultant features of folding on the Earth’s surface and make notes,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm on the meaning of folding and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views. Those with postural difficulties could require appropriate positioning,
2. Discuss types of folds resulting from tectonic forces and make presentations in class,
3. use print or digital resources to research on the resultant features of folding on the Earth’s surface and make notes,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Folding together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The skill of global awareness as the learner draws the world map showing the distribution of fold

mountains

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of making connections as the learner draws sketches of resultant features of

folding on the Earth’s surface

32

● Self-Efficacy: The skill of negotiation is enhanced as learners debate on the significance of folding and the

resultant features.

● Communication and Collaboration: The skill of teamwork and effective communication is enhanced as learners

discuss, in groups, types of folds resulting from tectonic forces and make presentations in class.

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology is enhanced as learners use print or digital resources to

research on the resultant features of folding on the Earth’s surface and make notes.

Values:
● Unity: Learner portrays team spirit as they take turns when brainstorming on the meaning of folding

● Respect: Learner displays humility as they discuss on types of folds resulting from tectonic forces

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner discusses on the types of folds resulting from tectonic forces

● Creativity: Learner draws the world map showing the distribution of fold mountains and display in class

● Assertiveness: Learner debates on the significance of folding and the resultant features

Suggested Learning Resources:

Photographs, pictures, local and extended environment, maps, realia, plain papers, manilla papers, plasticine, digital

resources, charts, marker pens, approved textbooks and other printed resources, library resources, whiteboards,

papier mache
